newsitem.title: THAILAND: Shinawatra 1997 outlook expected to be dull.
newsitem.headline: Shinawatra 1997 outlook expected to be dull.

text.p: The outlook for Thai conglomerate Shinawatra Computer and Communication Plc is expected to be poor this year because intensifying competition could cut into its profit margins, analysts said on Friday.

"For our view, the (Shinawatra) group's prospect is poor (in 1997) because (mobile phone) handset prices are going to come down very quickly," Paul Ngo, investment analyst at ING Baring, told Reuters.
Ngo said the bluechip Shinawatra's profit margin in 1997 was expected to drop to 20 percent from about 40 percent last year.

"The problem with the company is that in terms of handset prices the company is expected to see further margin deterioration in 1997 due to intensifying competition," said Michael Millar, research manager at Socgen-Crosby Securities.

Analysts expect the Shinawatra group to post a net profit of about three billion baht ($115.38 million) in 1996 and 2.9-3.3 billion baht in 1997. In 1995, the group posted a net profit of 3.3 billion baht.
Shinawatra reported a net profit of 2.41 billion baht in the first nine months of last year compared with 2.63 billion in the same period a year ago.
The company is scheduled to announce its 1996 result later this month.
Shinawatra Computer shares plunged to a three and a half year low on Thursday to close at 234 baht partly because the market dived to a four-and-half year low, brokers said.

Shinawatra Computer's weaker earnings in 1997 could also be compounded by slower growth of new mobile phone subscribers of its unit, Advanced Info Servicies Plc, amid stiffer competition, analysts said.

"The future of Advanced, we think, should not also be very good because of a lot of competition and Advanced has problems in expanding their analogue network. In terms of digital network TAC has a better network coverage," Ngo at ING Baring said.
Total Access Communication (TAC), majority owned by United Communication Industry Plc, is another big mobile phone operator in Thailand.
Millar said the cheaper mobile phone handset prices of Shinawatra Computer would reinvigorate Advanced Info's subscriber additions.
Analysts forecast Advanced Info's profit to be at about 3.5 billion baht in 1996 and 3.7 billion baht in 1997.
The company posted a net profit of 2.99 billion baht in 1995.
Advanced Info has contributed more than 60 percent to Shinawatra group's profit, analysts said.
